evidence: Hor. Ep. 1.1.25: aequē pauperibus prōdest, locuplētibus aequē (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Not destitute but of small means, “that has only enough for his moderate expenses” (Lewis & Short). As a noun, pauper, a poor man; pauperēs, the poor.

evidence: Plaut. Rud. 1.5.24: rēs pauperēs inopēsque (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: Rōmae quidem per sē hortus ager pauperis erat
phrases.english: at Rome the garden was the poor man’s field

phrases.latin: rūsticus urbānum mūrem mūs paupere fertur accēpisse cavō
phrases.english: a country mouse, they say, once welcomed a town mouse in his poor hole
it’s for a poor man to count his flock!

sources: Lewis & Short: pauper · Lewis & Short: inops · Lewis & Short: egeo
